key_insight: Photoacoustic imaging safely detected post-meal increases in intestinal blood flow in children, suggesting it can measure bowel vascular biomarkers noninvasively.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support earlier or more objective assessment of intestinal vascular health in pediatric conditions such as necrotizing enterocolitis.
method: 18 healthy pediatric participants were scanned with abdominal photoacoustic imaging before and after a lipid-rich snack.
Researchers manually outlined intestinal regions of interest in each abdominal quadrant.
They measured deoxygenated hemoglobin, oxygenated hemoglobin, total hemoglobin, and oxygen saturation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports minor, temporary adverse events and significant post-prandial hyperemia with no change in bowel oxygenation.
watch_item: Findings come from a small healthy pediatric cohort, so performance in sick infants and real-world NEC detection still needs validation.
paper_title: Photoacoustic imaging of intestinal physiological biomarkers in infants and children
